samples.summary: Route built by raw interpolation of a server-supplied slug (`/w/${slug}`) with no encoding; safe only because the backend currently constrains slugs
samples.evidence: `useDocumentsPath` returns `/w/${slug}` and the value is handed straight to `navigate()` in two places (`file-detail.tsx:132`, `file-shell.tsx:67`). I attempted a client-side route-confusion/open-redirect: a slug containing `//host`, `..`, `/settings`, `?` or `#` would change the resolved destination (react-router's `resolvePath` normalizes `..` segments, and `#`/`?` are parsed as hash/search). The attack is currently blocked upstream — `packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.dto.ts:30` restricts a caller-set slug to 1-64 lowercase alphanumerics/hyphens and `workspace.service.ts:22` generates slugs server-side — so I could not complete an exploit chain, hence low confidence. Worth `encodeURIComponent(slug)` here precisely because this hook is now the single reused definition of the destination: relaxing slug validation later (or a slug written by a seed/migration path that bypasses the DTO) would become a navigation-target injection at every call site at once.

samples.summary: Share token carried as a URL query parameter on a top-level-navigable blob URL, exposing it to history, Referer and access logs (pre-existing; this change documents and relies on that mount)
samples.evidence: `fileUrl(documentId, token)` appends `?token=<share-token>`; that URL is used by the viewer's fetch (`image-viewer.tsx:74`) and, more significantly, as a user-navigable `<a href>` at `shared-document.tsx:756`. The token is bearer-equivalent: `document-file.controller.ts:69-72` states a valid unexpired token alone authorizes reading the bytes. A token in a URL lands in browser history, in backend/proxy access logs, and is a Referer candidate for requests made from an inline-served document. Not introduced by this diff (which only adds `onClose` and the docs paragraph describing this anonymous mount) and partly mitigated because the share link itself already carries the token; a header-based share credential for the blob read would eliminate the extra copies. Reported for completeness, not as a regression.
